_comment: ⛔ QUARANTINED scene styles (five-line split, Aaron 2026-08-12): this dormant bench's style blocks, vendored OUT of ui_theme.json (a scene's values belong in its scene file). They move into this bench's own .scene.json at its migration — do not grow this file. Colors are $token refs into ui_theme.json's theme.tokens; a `theme` key here is refused as a palette fork.

sablework._comment: flicker-sablework 'Sablework Bench' HUD (hud_sablework.lua) — the texture SYNTHESIZER console. Three columns: LEFT the 6-voice CHANNEL RACK (per row: on-toggle, source pill, scale/octaves/warp sliders, blend pill, amount), CENTRE the tiled swatch preview + map selector, RIGHT the OUTPUT STAGE (relief/roughness/metalness/AO) over the selected voice's fine knobs. The preview RECT lives here under `preview` and is read by BOTH the Lua (which frames it) and the Rust scene (which draws the swatch sprites into it) — one source of truth, so the frame and the image cannot drift apart. Every colour is a $token and every label a stringtable $token (the one palette + one string source).

layout._comment: The bench rides the SHARED `workbench` template (ui_templates.json) like Clayworks and Loomforge — frame + header + tab bar + [viewport | rail] + footer. These are that template's slot dimensions; the frame's own chrome comes from the default `settings` style, which is why no window colours are redefined here.

preview._comment: The swatch. `tiles` is how many times the scene repeats the baked swatch per axis BEFORE uploading, so the seam is visible in one sprite node instead of nine. The Lua sizes the well; the scene reads `tiles` to build the image. w/h square, so the tiling reads honestly.
